---
title: "Quickstart"
guide-section: "Get started"
description: "From annotated examples to a prompt, and from model output back to spans."
---

This page walks through the whole loop: write annotated examples as CANE, build a few-shot
prompt, and parse what the model answers back into character spans.

## An annotated document

A `Document` is a text with entities. Each entity has one or more character spans and a
label:

```{python}
import cane_format as cane

text = "After starting amoxicillin, the patient developed a rash."
doc = cane.Document(
    text=text,
    entities=(
        cane.Entity(spans=[(15, 26)], label="DRUG"),
        cane.Entity(spans=[(52, 56)], label="ADR"),
    ),
)
[(e.label, text[e.start:e.end]) for e in doc.entities]
```

In practice you read documents from a corpus instead, for example with
`cane.read_brat("corpus/train")`.

## Write it as CANE

`dumps` writes the document in one of the four [variants](03-cane-format.qmd). Full adds an
anchor, a short verbatim snippet that tells the parser where the entity is:

```{python}
print(cane.dumps(doc, variant="full"))
```

## Build a prompt

`build_prompt` puts the task, the entity types, the guidelines and your examples in the
layout of the CANE paper, followed by the text to annotate:

```{python}
new_text = "Ibuprofen gave her a headache."
prompt = cane.build_prompt(new_text, examples=[doc], variant="full")
print(prompt[prompt.index("Examples:"):])  # the part after the guidelines
```

Send the prompt to any model; this library makes no model calls.

## Parse the answer

Suppose the model answers like this:

```{python}
output = """Entities:
`Ibuprofen` is a DRUG found in `Ibuprofen gave`
`headache` is a ADR found in `a headache.`
`nausea` is a ADR found in `and nausea`"""

result = cane.loads(output, text=new_text, variant="full", labels={"DRUG", "ADR"})
[(e.label, e.spans) for e in result.entities]
```

Problems never raise. They are collected in `result.issues`, one per line that could not be
grounded:

```{python}
for issue in result.issues:
    print(issue)
```

`result.ok` is `False` whenever there is an issue; `result.raise_for_errors()` turns them
into one exception if you prefer that.

## Save the result

Write the parsed document in any supported format, for example as brat to inspect it in an
annotation tool:

```python
result = cane.loads(output, text=new_text, variant="full", id="doc-17")
cane.write_brat([result.document], "predictions/")
```
